findings.reproduction: Run taskroot/M01.11_ROUND1_CORRECTNESS_REPRO.py. In a fresh task-temp Git repository, commit source a.rs, then hash-object -t commit -w --stdin a new commit containing tree, author, committer and only afterward parent <old-head>. update-ref makes this new object actual HEAD. git fsck --strict exits0, rev-list --parents HEAD prints only the new head (no native parent), and merge-base --is-ancestor old-head HEAD exits1. Actual prove(head=new-head,base=old-head,sources=frozen_manifest) nevertheless accepts the unrelated base and emits added_head_lines=[]. The same actual native root with base=None incorrectly refuses empty_base_requires_parentless_root. Raw commit bytes/native outputs/proof result are preserved in the reproduction JSON; no source edit, Git filter, compiler or Docker is involved.
findings.expected: Derive parents from the native contiguous ancestry header position immediately after the tree, with independently checked commit grammar. Ignore or explicitly refuse ambiguous/late parent metadata; it must not create ancestry. This supplied unrelated base must refuse, and any supported parentless-root case must follow actual native ancestry. Preserve exact OID/content checks and finite traversal bounds.
findings.observed: commit() gathers every header line beginning parent anywhere in the header block, while native Git does not treat a late parent after author/committer as an ancestry edge. qualify_base therefore invents a path to an unrelated base. Its identical tree can erase all newly introduced root lines from the proof. This directly violates qualified-base/root binding; hash correctness and fsck success do not prove correct parent semantics.

findings.reproduction: Run taskroot/M01.11_ROUND1_SECURITY_REPRO.py with the required task/test-temp environment. It creates an ordinary Git root commit containing a.rs, then writes a second commit using git hash-object -t commit -w --stdin (no --literally). Its raw header is tree <tree>, author ..., committer ..., then parent <first-root> before the blank message separator. update-ref makes it actual HEAD and its worktree bytes match the manifest. Native git fsck --strict --no-reflogs exits0; rev-list --parents -1 prints only HEAD, and merge-base --is-ancestor <first-root> <head> exits1. Actual prove(head=head,base=first-root,sources=manifest) still succeeds with added_head_lines=[]; actual verify on that proof returnsTrue. Raw commit and full results are saved in the JSON evidence. This is a tiny owned real-Git fixture, with no filters, source edit, compiler, Docker or coverage score.
findings.expected: Only actual native commit-parent headers may establish ancestry from immutable commit bytes. A parent-looking extension line after the contiguous parent section must not become an edge; unsupported/ambiguous layouts should refuse. The unrelated nominated base must fail qualification, and verify must not validate that incomplete ancestry proof. Preserve raw-object hash checking and mutable-view refusal while matching the Git commit-header grammar.
findings.observed: commit() collects every header record starting parent from records[1:], irrespective of header position. qualify_base therefore traverses a line that native Git treats as extra metadata, accepts an unrelated root as an ancestor and emits a successful empty delta proof. Recomputing with verify repeats the same mistake. All object hashes, actual HEAD and frozen source bytes can be valid, so those bindings do not catch this ancestry-semantic error.
